1.why: MFA endpoints call authorized(), which resolves the user only from the HttpOnly session cookie and never accepts a client-supplied user identifier.

2.why: Identity and OTP verification compare the submitted code against code stored in the caller's own session, not against a value shared across users.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets enabled=true and does not delete or invalidate other existing sessions, so previously issued sessions can continue to work.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext and backup codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes rather than plaintext.

5.why: Session IDs, CSRF tokens, OTP secrets, identity codes, and recovery codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session identifier is placed only in an HttpOnly Secure cookie and the client code does not write secrets, OTPs, or tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server-side regex and type checks validate email, phone, OTP, recovery code, manual secret, and CSRF data, although there is no separate explicit sanitization step.

8.why: Dynamic values inserted into the SPA are passed through an esc() function that HTML-encodes &, <, >, quotes, and apostrophes.

9.why: The only redirect is the fixed HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect to https://localhost:3000/, with no user-controlled redirect target.

10.why: Responses receive HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and a CSP that includes frame-ancestors protection.

11.why: The mfa_session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: The client-side log function writes backup recovery codes, and also OTP/test codes, to console and a visible logs panel, so those secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Identity codes expire and are marked used, TOTP verification prevents reuse within the current time window, and backup codes are marked used after acceptance.

14.why: Failed identity, TOTP, and recovery attempts increment session counters that lock the relevant verification flow after five failures.

15.why: The session ID is newly created after identity verification, sessions expire after idle and absolute limits, and logout deletes the session.
